clue.text: It's a lever used for many purposes

indicators.note: used in the sense of worked over or exploited, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a lever is a handy all-purpose tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges ITSALEVER (the letters of 'It's a lever'); the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adaptable enough to serve many different functions is described as versatile.

clue.text: Upset a seaman and soldiers, and mistakes occur

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the run of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of British soldiers

explanation.surface: A capsized sailor and some troops, with blunders following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' wants to read as an anagram signal, but in a down clue it turns the whole charade upside down, so the pieces are read in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural used for a list of printing errors found after publication.

clue.text: Divine French bag of scarlet hue

parts.note: sac is the French word for a bag
scarlet is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A heavenly French handbag in bright scarlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine and sacred are synonyms for holy, belonging to God.

explanation.surface: What a suitor has wanted up to this point.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor wants to go out with someone, to date them; the phrase also means up to the present moment.

explanation.surface: A computing term for a store of information.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'Data-base' looks like one computing term, but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowdown is slang for the inside information or facts; split in two it means low down, describing something base or mean.

indicators.note: out signals that the words before it are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors lay out a chart belonging to one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipmates are fellow sailors serving on the same vessel, so they are members of a crew.

clue.text: Stylish European goes to marsh for its seeds

indicators.note: goes to means the stylish European piece travels to and attaches after the marsh piece

parts.note: a fen is low, marshy land
U is the crossword abbreviation for upper-class, hence smart or stylish
a Greek is a European

explanation.surface: A fashionable Greek heads to the wetlands to gather seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: fenugreek is the herb grown for its seeds, used as a spice in curries.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenugreek is a Mediterranean plant cultivated mainly for its aromatic spice seeds.

indicators.note: embraced means the two outer pieces wrap around the word her

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible
a sage is wise

explanation.surface: A wise man from Scripture hugged a woman despite everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise can mean in any case or regardless, whatever the circumstances.

clue.text: Hold discussions about hospital in danger

indicators.note: about means the discussions word goes around the hospital abbreviation

parts.note: to treat is to negotiate or hold talks
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital on road signs

explanation.surface: Negotiators meeting over a hospital that is under threat.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a menace or risk of harm, the same idea as danger.

parts.note: crack as an adjective means top-class or expert, as in a crack shot
feeling down means feeling depressed

explanation.surface: A skilled person brought low by harsh policies.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown is a sudden firm enforcement action, such as a clampdown on protesters.

explanation.surface: A two-word note about a sharp bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is not a bargain but the timber: deal is softwood from fir or pine trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and trim in appearance; it is also a conifer whose pale softwood is sold as deal.

explanation.surface: A posted order calling troops to readiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Attention means notice or heed; it is also the upright stance a soldier adopts on the parade-ground command.

clue.text: The way to accommodate a bishop in school

indicators.note: to accommodate means the manner word gives room inside itself to the other pieces

parts.note: how means the way or manner in which
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A method for housing a bishop within a school.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROW is a famous English boarding school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow is a well-known English public school, attended by Churchill.

clue.text: Bosses of acerbic nature have the advantage

parts.note: heads are the bosses of organisations or schools
something tart is sharp or acerbic

explanation.surface: Sharp-tongued managers come out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an initial lead given or gained over rivals.

explanation.surface: Showing off a monocle.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking public show; the singular also once named a lens or eyeglass, as in a pair of spectacles.

clue.text: If Ted eats stew, he's full of woe

indicators.note: stew suggests a jumble cooked together, so the letters before it are mixed up

explanation.surface: Ted is miserable if he has to eat stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like the dish Ted eats but is the signal to rearrange IFTEDEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeatist expects failure, a gloomy pessimist always predicting the worst.

indicators.note: gets into means the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A child throwing a fit, as if bitten by a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so any insect such as this one is a six-footer.

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of predator

explanation.surface: A little hunter that is lethal from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a small venomous snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The asp is a small venomous Egyptian snake, famously deadly to Cleopatra.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Nat is the familiar short form of Nathan, the Hebrew prophet who rebuked King David

explanation.surface: Thugs assault an Old Testament prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat up' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Beat' defines, 'up' turns NAT round.
explanation.definitionFit: To tan someone, as in tanning their hide, means to thrash or beat them.

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
the press means reporters collectively

explanation.surface: A newspaper's long-serving reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Express is a British national daily newspaper; the 's in 'Paper's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Express is a British tabloid, so the title names a newspaper.

parts.note: in Oscar Wilde's novel Dorian Gray never grows older while his portrait decays, so he is a byword for unfading youth

explanation.surface: Comparing lasting qualities to Wilde's eternally young hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorian Gray keeps a youthful face for decades, never showing the passing years.

clue.text: Use it to cook betel leaf

explanation.surface: A tip on cooking with a betel leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan (or paan) is a South Asian preparation of betel leaf chewed after meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pan is a cooking vessel; pan is also the Indian name for the betel leaf.

clue.text: Ale and mint brew provides nourishment

indicators.note: brew means the words are mixed together as if being brewed, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drink of beer and mint supplies sustenance.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for food or nutriment.

clue.text: Tell little Richard to take a back seat

indicators.note: tell suggests speaking out, so the pet name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Dicky is a diminutive of Richard, via Dick

explanation.surface: Ordering a small boy named Richard to sit in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little Richard' suggests the rock singer, but is Dicky, the pet form of Richard. A dickey is the old folding rear seat of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A dickey or dickey seat is an extra folding seat at the back of a vintage car.

clue.text: Continue to dog school head guilty of prejudice

indicators.note: to dog is to follow closely, so this piece comes after the other
head means the first letter of the word school

parts.note: to exist is to continue to be

explanation.surface: A headteacher keeps being hounded for bias.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexist discriminates on grounds of gender, a form of prejudice.

explanation.surface: Protective barriers around royal soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Household Division's Guards regiments protect the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard is to shield or screen; the Guards are the regiments of the British sovereign's Household Division.

clue.text: She holds a big German gun

definitions.text: She holds a big German gun

parts.words: She holds a big German gun
parts.note: a woman's name is read as the nickname of the giant German howitzer of the First World War, so the woman is the gun

explanation.surface: A woman wielding a large German weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Bertha was the nickname of the huge Krupp siege howitzer used by Germany in 1914.

clue.text: Makes minute changes to fine melodies

parts.note: tunes are melodies

explanation.surface: A composer polishing some lovely music.
explanation.definitionFit: To fine-tune is to adjust something by tiny amounts for best performance.

indicators.note: avant-garde means experimental and unconventional, so the word artist is rearranged

explanation.surface: The qualities typical of a modernist painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avant-garde artist' reads as a pair; 'avant-garde' is the signal to rearrange ARTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Traits are characteristics or qualities, the features attributed to someone.

clue.text: Disparage poor Enid, and great trouble ensues

indicators.note: poor here means badly made or in a sorry state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Insult unfortunate Enid, and a big row follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges ENIDGREAT; 'trouble ensues' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To denigrate is to belittle or criticise unfairly.

explanation.surface: Being fond of a preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish is to enjoy greatly; a relish is also a spicy chutney or condiment.

parts.note: states means declares or asserts
a man is a he; the 's stands for 'is' and gives no letters

explanation.surface: Someone announces that he is a global leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman is a respected senior politician of international standing.
